blocks.orig: As you walk out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your personal Your Tanzania Trip guide greets you with a big smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' The guide takes you straight to your hotel, where you can relax and take in the African atmosphere. The next day your guide takes you on an exclusive, private safari that allows you to travel at your own pace. Enjoy the luxury of your own safari jeep and take the liberty to stop and watch the animals as long as you like!
blocks.html: When you step out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your personal Your Tanzania Trip guide is waiting with a broad smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' You are driven directly to your hotel, where you can unwind and soak up the African atmosphere. The following day your guide sets off with you on an exclusive, private safari, so you can travel at the pace that suits you. You have your own safari jeep, and you are free to stop and watch the animals for as long as you want.

blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is well known for its big groups of elephants and the huge amount of giant baobab trees. These trees can live for hundreds of years and are actually a source of water for elephants in the dry season as they have a special technique to draw water from them. Besides, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why in this season in Tarangire you can see groups of up to 250 elephants next to many more animals!
blocks.html: Large groups of elephants and a great many giant baobab trees are what Tarangire National Park is known for. The baobabs can live for hundreds of years, and in the dry season elephants actually use them as a water source, drawing water from them with a special technique. In the dry season the Tarangire River is also the only source of water, so at that time of year you can see groups of up to 250 elephants in Tarangire, along with many other animals!

blocks.orig: Experience the thrill of a night game drive in Tarangire National Park during your stay at Tarangire Safari Lodge. As twilight descends, venture into the wild and witness the vibrant nightlife of the African savanna. With expert guides leading the way, discover unique nocturnal wildlife and the mesmerizing sounds of nature. This unforgettable adventure allows you to see Tarangire’s diverse ecosystems in a new light. Don’t miss your chance to explore the wonders of Tanzania beneath the stars! Book your night game drive now!
blocks.html: While you stay at Tarangire Safari Lodge, you can enjoy the excitement of a night game drive in Tarangire National Park. When dusk falls, you head out into the wild to see the lively nightlife of the African savanna. Led by expert guides, you discover special nocturnal animals and the captivating sounds of nature. This memorable outing shows you Tarangire’s varied ecosystems in a different light. Take the chance to explore Tanzania under the stars and book your night game drive now!

blocks.orig: Lake Manyara National Park lies between Tarangire National Park and the Ngorongoro Crater, right along the 400 meters deep Great Rift Valley. The park boasts a variety of landscapes that attract many different animals. You can for example visit the lake that covers 75 percent of the park, pass through a dense rainforest with hundreds of monkeys and birds, and see elephants up close in the woodlands.
blocks.html: Between Tarangire National Park and the Ngorongoro Crater, right beside the 400 meters deep Great Rift Valley, you find Lake Manyara National Park. Its range of landscapes draws many different animals. You can, for instance, visit the lake that takes up 75 percent of the park, travel through dense rainforest full of hundreds of monkeys and birds, and get close to elephants in the woodlands.

blocks.orig: The village of Mto wa Mbu is a green oasis in between dry savannah plains, close to Lake Manyara National Park. A tuktuk can take a maximum of 3 people and a tour by tuktuk allows for maximum flexibility. Tuktuks can pass through small streets and can stop anywhere you like. The tour leads past the village itself, then into the forest and past several farms and plantations. In one or two hours you will stop at a brewery, a local artist and a local school.
blocks.html: Near Lake Manyara National Park, the village of Mto wa Mbu forms a green oasis between the dry savannah plains. A tuktuk seats up to 3 people, and touring by tuktuk gives you as much flexibility as possible. They fit through narrow streets and can stop wherever you want. The route takes you past the village, then into the forest and along several farms and plantations. Over one or two hours you stop at a brewery, a local artist and a local school.

blocks.orig: A visit to Lake Eyasi and the resident Hadzabe tribe makes for a fascinating daytrip. Lake Eyasi is a seasonal shallow salt lake south of the Ngorongoro Highlands, and a paradise for bird lovers. Spot hippos in the shallow waters, then take out your binoculars to spot for example the African spoonbill, flamingos, gray headed gulls, great white pelicans and pied avocets. Then visit the Hadzabe bushmen, masters in bow hunting.
blocks.html: A day trip to Lake Eyasi and the Hadzabe tribe who live there is a fascinating experience. South of the Ngorongoro Highlands, Lake Eyasi is a shallow, seasonal salt lake and a paradise for bird lovers. Look for hippos in the shallow water, then pick up your binoculars to find species such as the African spoonbill, flamingos, gray headed gulls, great white pelicans and pied avocets. After that you meet the Hadzabe bushmen, masters of bow hunting.

blocks.orig: The famous Ngorongoro Crater is one of Africa's seven natural wonders. The crater was formed two million years ago when a vast volcano erupted. The fertile lava has created a unique ecosystem, now home to the highest concentration of animals found anywhere in Africa! Once in the crater, thousands of animals such as lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos surround you, and the views are astounding – you won’t know where to look!
blocks.html: The well-known Ngorongoro Crater is counted among Africa's seven natural wonders. It was created two million years ago when a huge volcano erupted. The fertile lava produced a unique ecosystem that is now home to the highest concentration of animals anywhere in Africa! Inside the crater you are surrounded by thousands of animals, including lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos, and the views are so striking you won’t know where to look first!

blocks.orig: Immerse yourself in the culture, colors, and traditions of the Maasai, go on a journey through time and experience how people can be satisfied with the simplest way of life. Learn about their survival skills and what their everyday life looks like in and around their village homes. A unique experience you don't want to miss during your Tanzania trip!
blocks.html: Step into the culture, colours and traditions of the Maasai, travel back in time and see how people can be content with the simplest way of living. Find out about their survival skills and what daily life is like in and around the homes of their village. A special experience not to miss on your Tanzania trip!

blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park is widely known as the place to go on safari, mainly because of the Great Migration that passes through here. The enormous, stampeding herds are impressive, as are the vast number of predators that live here: over four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas, and hundreds of wild dogs! And of course, plenty of other beautiful animals, which your guide will be delighted to search for together with you. Are you ready for this?
blocks.html: Serengeti National Park is famous as the place for a safari, largely because of the Great Migration that moves through it. The huge stampeding herds are impressive, and so is the number of predators living here: more than four thousand lions, more than 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas and hundreds of wild dogs! There are of course many other beautiful animals too, and your guide will gladly look for them with you. Are you ready?

blocks.orig: A balloon safari in the iconic Serengeti National Park will make your Tanzania safari a memorable experience. You rise at sunrise and gently fly over the endless plains of the Serengeti. The hot air balloon floats at treetop height above the baobabs and acacias so that you can see the animals nearby. Watching the wildlife below from your balloon is a fascinating and peaceful experience that comes with breathtaking panoramic views.
blocks.html: Taking a balloon safari over the iconic Serengeti National Park turns your Tanzania safari into an experience to remember. You go up at sunrise and drift slowly across the vast Serengeti plains. The balloon glides at treetop height over the baobabs and acacias, so you can see the animals close by. Looking down on the wildlife from the balloon is a captivating and calm experience, with stunning views all around.

blocks.orig: From late December through March, the Ndutu region becomes the heart of the Great Migration, as over 2 million animals arrive to give birth. The Ndutu region straddles the southern part of the Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. The short, nutrient-rich grass makes the area a haven for newborn zebras and wildebeests, but also a prime spot for predators. This seasonal gathering creates close-up wildlife sightings and constant activity across the plains.
blocks.html: Between late December and March, the Ndutu region is the centre of the Great Migration, when more than 2 million animals come here to give birth. The region spans the southern Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Thanks to the short, nutritious grass, the area is a safe place for newborn zebras and wildebeests, and also an ideal hunting ground for predators. This seasonal gathering means close wildlife encounters and non-stop activity on the plains.

blocks.orig: The last day! Depending on your flight time, you can relax in the lodge a bit longer before heading to Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) for your flight home. Having second thoughts? It's also possible to add a few days to your holiday by going to one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day! Depending on when your flight leaves, you can relax at the lodge a little longer before you travel to Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) for your flight home. Not ready to leave yet? You can also add a few days to your holiday on one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia!
